findings.description: Adding a `paths:` frontmatter block turns stash-safety.md from an always-loaded rule into a path-conditional one (loaded only when the model works with *.sh, *.bats, .claude/scripts or .claude/hooks files). The rule governs `git stash push/pop` shapes typed into Bash, which happen regardless of which files are being edited. In the common case (editing app code, then running `git stash pop | tail -1`) the prose guard is now absent.
findings.failure_mode: The prose layer behind the floor fence FR-1.2b stops reaching the model in most sessions; only the harness regex remains, and the broader guidance (do not wrap skill execution in stash) no longer applies to the sessions that most need it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `paths:` from stash-safety.md (keep it always-on), or add a broad pattern such as `**/*` if the frontmatter fields origin/version/enacted_by are the only goal of the change.

findings.description: The implementing-tasks skill's declared app-zone permission is widened from `read` to `read-write`. This is unrelated to the guard register / task-kinds scope of the PR and is not explained in the diff. skill-invariants.md (also in this diff) documents zones as the path-level control for app-code writes, so anything that reads `zones.app.permission` (validate-skill-capabilities.sh, future implement-gate work) now sees a different declaration for the one skill that writes app code.
findings.failure_mode: If any validator or gate consumes the zones frontmatter, the implementing skill silently gains write permission on src/lib/app without an audited decision; if nothing consumes it, the change is undocumented drift in a security-relevant declaration.
findings.suggested_fix: Either revert the hunk, or move it to its own change with a DEC row and a note in skill-invariants.md explaining why /implement's app zone is read-write while the glossary says the App zone needs confirmation before a write.

findings.cross_file_justification: guard-origins.yaml (in diff) marks policy:permission-deny-list, policy:operator-only-commands and 16 fence:FR-SZ* rows as floor, but floor.yaml (in diff) pins only indirect artefacts for them.
findings.description: floor_files pins .claude/hooks/settings.deny.json and .claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt, but the enforced artefacts are the deny list inside .claude/settings.json and the `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter of each operator-only command file; neither is in floor_files. Likewise all FR-SZ/FR-SZ2 fence rows are `floor: true` while .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh (their implementation) is not pinned; only the corpus rows under floor_corpus protect them, and tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh is itself modified in this PR and not pinned. floor_keys also lists `implement_gate.*` while gate:implement-gate and hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh are `floor: false`.
findings.failure_mode: A cycle task can remove deny entries from settings.json, strip `disable-model-invocation` from a command, or loosen an FR-SZ regex while floor-snapshot.bats and guard-origins.bats both pass, so the floor advertises protection it does not provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .claude/settings.json (or a test that diffs its permissions.deny against settings.deny.json), a test that cross-checks user-invoked-commands.txt against command frontmatter, and tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/run-corpus.sh to floor_files; either mark gate:implement-gate floor or drop implement_gate.* from floor_keys so the two lists agree.
